property.text: In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021), each cell_index MUST be strictly less than CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. Out-of-range cell_indices MUST be rejected before being used in coset_for_cell or coset_shift_for_cell.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends cell_indices >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB via P2P. coset_shift_for_cell and coset_for_cell access roots_brp[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index], which would be out-of-bounds.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds array access in coset_shift_for_cell or coset_for_cell could crash the node (segfault) or cause memory corruption, leading to single-node DoS.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating node crash from out-of-range cell_index in P2P data column sidecar.

property.text: In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021), each commitment_bytes MUST have length exactly BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT, each cell MUST have length exactly BYTES_PER_CELL, and each proof_bytes MUST have length exactly BYTES_PER_PROOF. Incorrect lengths MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: Incorrect byte lengths from P2P could cause deserialization errors, buffer overflows, or incorrect field element parsing.

property.severity_justification: Accepting incorrectly-sized bytes could cause buffer overflows or incorrect deserialization, potentially leading to crashes or memory corruption.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating crash or unexpected behavior from malformed byte lengths.

property.text: bytes_to_kzg_commitment and bytes_to_kzg_proof MUST perform BLS12-381 G1 subgroup checks during deserialization. Points not on the correct subgroup MUST be rejected. Accepting non-subgroup points would cause the pairing check to produce incorrect results.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides commitment or proof bytes that deserialize to a point on the BLS12-381 curve but NOT in the correct G1 subgroup. Without subgroup checks, the pairing equation could give incorrect results.

property.severity_justification: Missing subgroup checks in pairing-based cryptography is a well-known class of vulnerability. It allows forging proofs that pass the pairing check, breaking data availability guarantees.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with a non-subgroup point that causes the pairing check to accept an invalid proof.

property.text: In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021), commitment deduplication MUST preserve semantic equivalence: forall k: deduplicated_commitments[commitment_indices[k]] == original_commitment_bytes[k]. The mapping from original indices to deduplicated indices MUST be bijective on equivalence classes.

reachability.notes: An off-by-one in the commitment_indices mapping would cause weights to be accumulated against the wrong commitment in the verification equation.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect commitment-to-index mapping causes verification to aggregate weights incorrectly, potentially accepting invalid proofs.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a batch with deliberately structured commitments that exploit an off-by-one in the mapping.

property.text: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) MUST require at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells for recovery. If fewer than 50% of cells are provided, the function MUST reject the input. This threshold is mathematically required by the rate-2 Reed-Solomon erasure coding.

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

property.severity_justification: Bypassing the 50% threshold produces a mathematically incorrect recovered polynomial, which then generates incorrect cells and proofs that propagate through the network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing recovery with fewer than 50% cells produces incorrect output that is accepted downstream.

property.text: In recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024), cell_indices MUST be unique and in ascending sorted order. Duplicate cell_indices MUST be rejected. forall i < j: cell_indices[i] < cell_indices[j].

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

property.severity_justification: Duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data would cause polynomial recovery to produce an incorrect polynomial, leading to distribution of invalid data.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with duplicate cell_indices and conflicting cells causing incorrect recovery.

property.text: In recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024), all cell_indices MUST be in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Out-of-range indices MUST be rejected before polynomial recovery begins.

reachability.notes: Out-of-range cell indices would cause out-of-bounds access in coset computation functions.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds cell indices cause crashes in coset_for_cell and related functions, leading to single-node DoS.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating node crash from out-of-range cell_index during recovery.

property.text: After recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) produces a recovered polynomial, the caller MUST verify the recovered cells and proofs against the original KZG commitment. The recovery function itself does NOT verify commitment consistency. forall recovered_cell: verify_cell_kzg_proof(original_commitment, cell_index, recovered_cell, recovered_proof) == True.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides corrupted cells for valid cell_indices. Without post-recovery commitment verification, the node propagates incorrect data to other peers.

property.severity_justification: Missing post-recovery verification turns a validator node into a vector for distributing invalid data. Other nodes trusting reconstructed data accept corrupted cells.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a node distributing corrupted cells after recovery from attacker-provided data without commitment re-verification.

property.text: The recovered polynomial from recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) MUST have degree strictly less than FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. The output poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] truncation MUST not discard any non-zero coefficients above FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB.

reachability.notes: If the recovered polynomial has degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, the truncation discards non-zero coefficients, producing an incorrect polynomial.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect truncation produces wrong cells and proofs. However, this should be caught by post-recovery commitment verification.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating crafted cell data that causes the recovered polynomial to exceed the expected degree.

property.text: In recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023), the element-wise division reconstructed[i] = ez_over_coset[i] / zp_over_coset[i] MUST NOT encounter division by zero. The vanishing polynomial Z(x) evaluated on the coset (shifted by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY) MUST be non-zero at every point. forall i: zp_over_coset[i] != 0.

reachability.notes: The coset shift by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY ensures Z(x) has no roots on the coset. If the shift is incorrect, division by zero crashes the node.

property.severity_justification: Division by zero during recovery crashes the validator node. Although the root cause is an incorrect coset shift (implementation bug), the trigger is attacker-controlled cell withholding.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a division-by-zero crash during cell recovery triggered by specific missing cell patterns.
